framework_status: Proposed (pre-publication), first empirical validation on a real project
assessment_subject: FIBEMATE v3.3.0 — Post-Quantum Cryptography Full-Stack Engineering Platform

d1_algorithm_interface_abstraction.description: Whether algorithms are invoked through abstract interfaces vs direct implementation calls
d1_algorithm_interface_abstraction.finding: Zero abstraction layer. All call sites directly invoke concrete implementations: SM2.generateKeypair(), MLKEM.encapsulate(), etc.

direct_calls.hybrid_kem_client_js: 14+ direct SM2.xxx / MLKEM.xxx invocations (L111, L135, L163, L224, L260, L306-317)
direct_calls.pq_integration_js: Partial abstraction — PQDoubleRatchet wraps ML-KEM but still imports it directly
direct_calls.security_levels_js: Defines 6 security levels but does not map to concrete algorithm providers
direct_calls.ml_kem_768_wrapper_js: Thin pass-through wrapper, not an interface abstraction

d1_algorithm_interface_abstraction.root_cause: Educational design: direct SM2.computeDHKey() is clearer to read than KeyExchangeProvider.derive(keyMaterial). Abstraction would add a layer of indirection that obscures the algorithm internals.
d1_algorithm_interface_abstraction.improvement_hypothetical: Add AlgorithmRegistry → SM2.validateNegotiation(offer) instead of direct generateKeypair

d2_algorithm_configuration_externalizati.description: Whether algorithm parameters are externally configurable vs hardcoded
d2_algorithm_configuration_externalizati.finding: Zero external configuration files. All parameters hardcoded as const in source.

hardcoded_params.hybrid_kem_client_js_L38_44: IANA_GROUP_ID=4590, SM2_PK_LEN=65, MLKEM_PK_LEN=1184, CT=1088, SS=32, HYBRID=64

good_practice_sole_exception.fml_dsa_paramset: sign(sk, msg, ctx, paramSet) — paramSet is a runtime function argument enabling ML-DSA-44/65/87 switching. This is the ONLY externally configurable algorithm parameter in the entire codebase.

d2_algorithm_configuration_externalizati.root_cause: All parameters are algorithmic constants derived from NIST FIPS standards — intended to be immutable for correctness, not flexibility.
d2_algorithm_configuration_externalizati.improvement_hypothetical: config.json { algorithms: { ml-kem: { N:256, K:3, Q:3329 } } } — single-source-of-truth

d3_algorithm_version_management.description: Whether multiple algorithm versions can coexist and be identified
d3_algorithm_version_management.finding: Multiple implementations exist for some algorithms, but without version registry or deprecation markers. File-based backup (.v1.3-backup) is the only versioning mechanism.

sm2.versioning: sm2-bigint-ec.js.v1.3-backup — file rename backup, no git tag or semver

ml_kem.note: Different algorithms (768 vs 1024), not 'same algorithm different versions'

ml_dsa.note: Noble used for cross-validation only, not officially supported

d3_algorithm_version_management.historical_context: SM2 multi-track is an artifact of implementation evolution (jsbn → BigInt migration), not a designed versioning strategy.

d4_key_format_coupling.description: Whether key/certificate serialization formats are decoupled from algorithm specifics
d4_key_format_coupling.finding: Key serialization formats deeply bind to algorithm parameters. No Format abstraction layer to negotiate key lengths.

format_bindings.ml_kem_768_pk: 1184B = byteEncode(t_hat, 12) + ρ — hardcoded sizes tied to (N=256, K=3, d=12)
format_bindings.sm2_pk: 65B uncompressed point (04||x||y) — tied to SM2 curve
format_bindings.iana_4590_key_share: 2B group_id || 2B sm2_pk_len || SM2_pk(65B) || MLKEM_pk(1184B) — custom binary concatenation
format_bindings.opk_key_id: Simple integer ID — decoupled from key content (sole positive)

no_format_abstraction: No KeyFormat interface to negotiate length/encoding
Buffer size assumptions scattered across files
d4_key_format_coupling.impact: To upgrade ML-KEM-768→1024: must change ALL code reading/writing 1184-byte buffers → ~40-60 lines across multiple files
d4_key_format_coupling.improvement_hypothetical: KeyFormat.deserialize(algo, buffer) → returns {type, key, length} regardless of algorithm

d5_protocol_negotiation_capability.description: Whether runtime algorithm negotiation (capability exchange) is supported
d5_protocol_negotiation_capability.finding: Protocol negotiation is effectively a parameter declaration, not capability negotiation. Single-algorithm offers with zero fallback.

negotiation_patterns.gm_js_L183_197: negotiateWithServer() sends { algorithm:'SM2' } — single option, no alternatives
negotiation_patterns.hybrid_kem_client: SM2+MLKEM-768 fixed combination, no cipher suite list

no_negotiation_support: No custom cipher suite capability list
No fallback negotiation ('try ML-KEM-1024, fallback to ML-KEM-768')

partial_good_practice.message_gm_js: Supports AES-GCM/SM4-GCM switch, but the decision is caller-side, not negotiated

d5_protocol_negotiation_capability.root_cause: Educational design: showing 'SM2 + ML-KEM-768 hybrid handshake' is clearest with the full path hardcoded. TLS negotiation state machines would obscure the core algorithm interaction.

d6_algorithm_replacement_cost.description: Lines of code and files changed to replace one algorithm with another
d6_algorithm_replacement_cost.finding: Algorithm replacement requires touching 7-11 files and re-running full test suites. Only fml-dsa supports runtime switching.

ml_kem_768_to_1024.lines_to_change: ~40-60 (12 constants + byteEncode logic + buffer sizes + matVecMul dimensions)

ml_dsa_65_to_87.note: Runtime parameter switch — best practice in codebase

d6_algorithm_replacement_cost.sole_good_practice: fml-dsa runtime parameter set switching (ML-DSA-44/65/87 via function argument) — implemented with later design maturity

d7_observability.description: Whether current algorithm usage is monitorable, auditable, and detectable
d7_observability.finding: Offline observability (CI/TSR/KAT/TVLA) is industry-leading. Runtime observability (monitoring, audit logging, anomaly detection) is zero.

offline_observability.code_integrity: 8 CI/CD workflows (ci, ci-native, native-build, nightly-phase1, nightly-phase2, release, repolinter, scorecard) — every push
offline_observability.cryptographic_correctness: TSR evidence chain lg-001~100 (DigiCert + FreeTSA dual authority), 100 timestamp records
offline_observability.performance: benchmark.cjs + perf-gate.js (WARN 20%, FAIL 50%) — every CI run

runtime_observability.monitoring: None — no runtime algorithm usage tracking
runtime_observability.audit_logging: None — no per-session algorithm audit trail

d7_observability.key_insight: TSR evidence chain is post-hoc verification ('this version of code was correct'), not runtime monitoring ('is the running code being tampered with?'). Verification platform observability = test suite output, not dashboard metrics.
d7_observability.improvement_hypothetical: Runtime instrumentation: session.algorithms = { kex:'MLKEM768', sign:'FMLDSA65' } with TSR-anchored audit log

comparison_with_cars.gap_explanation: CARS is an organizational maturity framework (measuring 'does the org have policy X?'). IBM is a code-level decoupling framework (measuring 'is the API layer algorithm-agnostic?'). FIBEMATE scores higher on organizational readiness (docs/CI/TSR) than code decoupling (hardcoded algorithm calls). This gap is not a contradiction — it precisely quantifies the 'executable textbook' position: documentation and process are mature, but code deliberately avoids abstraction layers for pedagogical clarity.

dimension_comparison.inventory: CARS=85 vs IBM=N/A — CARS measures what you have, IBM doesn't measure inventory
dimension_comparison.agility: CARS=40 vs IBM_spread=(25+15)=low — IBM splits agility into two finer dimensions, both scoring lower
dimension_comparison.key_lifecycle: CARS=70 vs IBM=35 — CARS sees TLA+ formal verification as a plus, IBM sees hardcoded buffer sizes
dimension_comparison.protocol_coupling: CARS=55 vs IBM=20 — CARS sees 'intentional educational decoupling', IBM sees 'zero cipher suite negotiation'
dimension_comparison.org_readiness: CARS=60 vs IBM=65 — IBM's observability dimension discovers CI/TSR coverage is higher than CARS gives credit for

improvement_roadmap.item: Create config.json as single source of truth for algorithm parameters

framework_feedback: Interface abstraction ≠ code quality: FIBEMATE's SM2.generateKeypair() direct call is a pedagogical virtue, but IBM framework penalizes it as coupling. Suggest adding 'abstraction appropriateness' sub-dimension to distinguish intentional educational coupling from accidental tight coupling.
Observability should distinguish offline/online: IBM framework does not differentiate CI/KAT/TSR post-hoc evidence from runtime Prometheus/dashboard monitoring. Both serve different security goals.

Configuration externalization needs hardware exemption: FPGA NTT parameters cannot be 'externalized' because they are synthesized into silicon. Suggest adding hardware platform exemption for embedded/FPGA targets.
methodology_note: All assessment data sourced from FIBEMATE public engineering data. No new tests were run. All code references include file paths and line numbers. IBM framework scoring criteria are derived from the framework's stated principles — since this framework may not have published a final scoring rubric, this report should be treated as an empirical validation proposal, not a definitive rating.
